label: Murciélagos Special Forces Airlift — Santa Lucía to Culiacán (Jun 3, 2026)
notes: 90 members of Mexico's elite Fuerzas Especiales del Ejército (Los Murciélagos) airlifted from Military Air Base No. 1 in Santa Lucía, Estado de México, to the Culiacán military air base aboard a Boeing 737/800 on June 3, 2026. Deployed in response to 10 homicides in Culiacán that day and 30 deaths in the preceding 72 hours. Defense Secretary Trevilla Trejo and National Guard Commander Briseño Lobera visited Culiacán the following day for emergency supervisory review.

label: El Mayo's Extradition Flight — Culiacán to El Paso (Jul 25, 2024)
notes: Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada sedated and flown from Huertos del Pedregal ranch near Culiacán to a private airfield near Santa Teresa, New Mexico (near El Paso) where DEA agents took custody.

label: La Mayiza Opening Strike — Los Mochis to Culiacán (Sep 9, 2024)
notes: Synchronized La Mayiza strikes launched from northern strongholds against Chapitos positions in Culiacán. Field commander El Comanche coordinated attacks along this corridor.

label: Chapitos Highway 15 North — Culiacán to Choix
notes: Los Chapitos' claimed control corridor along Highway 15 northbound from Culiacán through El Fuerte to the Chihuahua border. Armed checkpoints documented throughout this route.

label: CJNG Incursion — Durango to Sinaloa Border (Early 2025)
notes: CJNG gunmen deployed from Durango into the Sinaloa-Durango border zone to support Los Chapitos. Hundreds of CJNG fighters moved along this mountain corridor to engage La Mayiza-affiliated groups.

label: Chapitos Fentanyl Route — Culiacán to Sonora Border
notes: Primary northbound trafficking route for Chapitos-processed fentanyl from Culiacán production facilities toward the US border crossings in Sonora. The Chapitos imposed licensing requirements on independent fentanyl producers in 2024.

label: La Mayiza Pacific Corridor — Los Mochis to Mazatlán
notes: La Mayiza's primary Pacific coast control corridor linking northern strongholds to southern Sinaloa. The faction moved to contest Mazatlán's lucrative criminal plaza throughout 2025, driving a 227% homicide increase.

label: Military Reinforcement — Mexico City to Culiacán
notes: Route of Army reinforcements sent by President Sheinbaum after taking office. Ultimately 11,000–14,000 soldiers were deployed to Sinaloa and surrounding states. Security Secretary García Harfuch personally traveled to Culiacán in June 2025.

label: Chapitos Retreat to Sierra — Culiacán to Badiraguato
notes: As La Mayiza gained the upper hand in Culiacán, Los Chapitos regrouped and moved fighters up into Badiraguato and the Sierra Madre strongholds historically associated with El Chapo's family.

label: Displacement Flow — Badiraguato to Culiacán
notes: Route taken by thousands of displaced rural families fleeing violence in Badiraguato, Concordia, Cosalá and other sierra municipalities. Most headed to Culiacán or Mazatlán seeking safety.

label: Displacement — Concordia to Mazatlán
notes: Route taken by approximately 180–200 El Palmito residents and hundreds more from Concordia municipality. Mazatlán absorbed most displaced persons from southern Sinaloa, straining city social services.

label: La Mayiza Sierra Advance — May 2025
notes: La Mayiza's advance through the Sierra Madre Occidental in May 2025, capturing communities including Surutato, Los Sitios, and La Apoma. This effectively eliminated the last Chapitos mountain strongholds.

label: Chapitos Mazatlán Supply Route
notes: Chapitos-controlled corridor from Culiacán south to Mazatlán. La Mayiza's contest of this route contributed to the dramatic increase in Mazatlán violence during 2025.

label: Displaced Producers Route — Los Mochis to Sonora
notes: Route taken by independent fentanyl producers pushed out of Sinaloa after the Chapitos imposed licensing requirements in late 2024. Producers relocated to Sonora and Baja California to work with semi-independent Sinaloa-affiliated groups closer to the US border.

label: Chapo Isidro Forces — Guasave to Culiacán
notes: Deployment corridor for Fausto 'Chapo Isidro' Meza Flores and his Vitache Special Forces moving south from Guasave territory to reinforce La Mayiza positions in the Culiacán battle zone.

label: Pacific Maritime Corridor — Topolobampo to Mazatlán
notes: Pacific maritime drug export route linking Topolobampo deep-water port (near Los Mochis) to Mazatlán port. Used by La Mayiza for bulk drug exports to Asian and Latin American markets.

label: Golden Triangle Supply Route — Sierra to Culiacán
notes: Traditional route moving drugs produced in the Golden Triangle (Sinaloa-Chihuahua-Durango sierra) down to Culiacán processing and distribution centers. Contested throughout the civil war.

label: Navy Raid — SEMAR Base to El Patas Capture Site (Mar 19, 2026)
notes: Route of Mexican Navy forces from the Culiacán naval base to the location where plaza boss El Patas was captured. 11 killed in the operation. Short but decisive urban operation demonstrating SEMAR's intelligence-driven capability.

label: Joaquín Guzmán López's Voluntary Surrender Flight (Jul 25, 2024)
notes: Route of Joaquín Guzmán López's flight from Culiacán area to El Paso where he surrendered voluntarily to US authorities alongside the kidnapped El Mayo. His cooperation with US prosecutors pre-dated the event.

label: DEA Enforcement Arc — Culiacán to US Operations
notes: Conceptual arc representing the DEA's coordinated August 2025 operation spanning 23 US field divisions targeting Sinaloa Cartel supply chains. 617 arrested, half-ton of fentanyl seized.

label: Ovidio Guzmán Extradition — Guadalajara to Chicago
notes: Ovidio Guzmán López was extradited from Mexico to Chicago where he pleaded guilty to drug conspiracy charges in July 2025 and agreed to cooperate. His cooperation agreement undermines Chapitos leadership cohesion.

label: La Mayiza Southern Sweep — Los Mochis to Concordia
notes: La Mayiza's territorial consolidation drive along the Pacific slopes from northern Sinaloa through Elota, San Ignacio, and into Concordia. This advance pushed Chapitos forces back to mountain strongholds.

label: Escuinapa Ambush — Mazatlán–Tepic Highway (Mar 31, 2026)
notes: Corridor on the Mazatlán–Tepic highway where a cartel hit squad ambushed 4 Escuinapa municipal police officers on March 31, 2026. Subdirector Gutiérrez Mazariegos killed. Cartel activity intensifying in the Sinaloa–Nayarit border zone despite Semana Santa security surge.

label: SEMAR Cosalá Lab Raid — Navy Base to La Palma (Apr 3, 2026)
notes: Route of Mexican Navy (SEMAR) forces raiding a Chapitos-linked clandestine meth lab in La Palma, Cosalá, on April 3, 2026. Seized 1,000 liters of P2P precursor. No armed confrontation. Continues pattern of intelligence-driven SEMAR operations following the March 19 El Patas capture.

label: Escuinapa Special Operation — 1,190 Troops Deployed (Apr 10, 2026)
notes: Governor Rubén Rocha Moya deployed 1,190 state police, National Guard, and Mexican Army personnel from Culiacán to Escuinapa, Rosario, and Concordia municipalities on April 10, 2026. Response to 5 officers killed in 9 days and the mass resignation of 32 Escuinapa officers (~40% of the force). A permanent Joint Operations Base was established in Escuinapa to cover the security vacuum.

label: US State Dept Visa Restrictions — 75 Sinaloa Cartel Associates (Apr 20, 2026)
notes: Secretary Rubio announced visa restrictions on 75 family members and close associates of Sinaloa Cartel-sanctioned persons under EO 14059 on April 20, 2026. Conceptual arc representing the reach of US financial and diplomatic enforcement against the Sinaloa Cartel network. Followed the April 14 ICE $10M reward for Iván Archivaldo and the April 16 $10M bounty doubling for El Mochomito — a coordinated week of maximum US pressure on the Chapitos.

label: Escuinapa–Teacapán: 5 Chapitos Arrested (Apr 16, 2026)
notes: Joint federal operation (SSPC, SEDENA, FGR, National Guard with aerial support) intercepted a Chapitos vehicle on the Escuinapa–Teacapán highway in southern Sinaloa on April 16, 2026. Five operatives detained; seized 7 long-barrel firearms, 6 ballistic vests, 1 vehicle. The corridor is contested between La Mayiza and Chapitos remnants pushing toward Nayarit. Line represents the general federal security operation axis from Culiacán to southern Sinaloa.

label: CIA–AEI Sierra Tarahumara Drug Lab Raid — Crash Site (Apr 21, 2026)
notes: Conceptual route of the joint CIA–Chihuahua AEI counter-narcotics operation in the Sierra Tarahumara, Morelos municipality, Chihuahua (Golden Triangle adjacent). The team destroyed six clandestine drug labs on April 20, then died in a vehicle crash on the mountain road while returning. Two CIA officers and two Mexican AEI officials killed. President Sheinbaum demanded investigation; the operation was conducted without federal government notification. Connects the Sinaloa theater to the Golden Triangle drug production zone in Chihuahua.

label: Federal El Guano Operation — Culiacán to Badiraguato (Apr 22, 2026)
notes: Route of major federal security operation targeting Aureliano 'El Guano' Guzmán Loera (El Chapo's brother, La Mayiza sierra commander) in Badiraguato/Golden Triangle on April 22, 2026. Deployed 5 UH-60 Black Hawk helicopters, Beechcraft T-6 Texan II aircraft, National Guard, and Marine elements from Culiacán. Security Secretary García Harfuch confirmed 'detainees' but refused to name them. SEDENA officially denied El Guano's capture on April 23 — he evaded for the fourth time. Also targeted huachicol (fuel theft) networks under El Guano's protection.

label: SEDENA/SEMAR Tamazula Operation — 10 Gente del Guano Arrested (Apr 23, 2026)
notes: Second federal operation against El Guano on April 23, 2026, shifting from Badiraguato to Tamazula (Sinaloa-Durango border). Joint SEDENA/SEMAR forces with US intelligence support arrested 10 members of the Gente del Guano faction including El Guano's right-hand man 'Abel N', chief bodyguard, and financial/logistics operator. Weapons, ammunition, and explosive devices seized. El Guano evaded for the fourth time. Line represents the Culiacán-based federal forces' operational arc toward the Tamazula sierra zone.

label: US Treasury OFAC — 23-Person Fentanyl Precursor Network Sanctioned (Apr 24, 2026)
notes: US Treasury OFAC on April 24, 2026 sanctioned 23 individuals and entities in a transnational fentanyl precursor supply network (India, Guatemala, Mexico) with direct ties to the Sinaloa Cartel (FTO). The network supplied 4-Piperidone and N-Boc-4-Piperidone to Sinaloa cartel labs — 1 kg of N-Boc-4-Piperidone yields ~1.83 kg of fentanyl (~900,000 lethal doses). Coordinated with a State Department statement on countering the transnational supply chain. Part of a sustained week of US pressure (Apr 20: visa restrictions on 75 associates; Apr 24: OFAC sanctions). Conceptual arc Washington DC to Culiacán representing US financial enforcement reach against Sinaloa Cartel supply chains.

label: Displacement Flow — Culiacán to Durango 'El Culiacancito' (2025–2026)
notes: Route of internal displacement of Culiacán families fleeing cartel violence to Durango City, where they have concentrated in southeastern neighborhoods dubbed 'El Culiacancito' by locals. Documented by Revista Espejo (April 25, 2026) and N+: rents up 50%+ over 12 months, school enrollment surges from September 2025, newcomers opening businesses. Represents the conflict's geographic footprint beyond Sinaloa state borders. Sits alongside the existing Badiraguato→Culiacán displacement flow. 88.1% of Culiacán residents feel unsafe per the National Urban Security Survey (ENSU).

label: Sheinbaum Sovereignty Response — Mexico City to Culiacán (May 1–3, 2026)
notes: Conceptual arc from Mexico City (federal executive) to the Sinaloa state congress in Culiacán, representing the political crisis triggered by the April 30 DOJ SDNY indictment. May 1: President Sheinbaum invoked sovereignty, refused extradition of Rocha Moya without 'irrefutable evidence,' ordered independent probe. May 2: Governor Rocha Moya took temporary leave via video; Mayor Gámez Mendívil resigned (losing immunity). May 3: Sinaloa legislature appointed Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde as interim governor — Mexico's institutional response to the first US federal indictment of a sitting Mexican state governor.

label: DOJ SDNY Indicts Sinaloa Governor + 9 Officials — Historic Chapitos Corruption Charges (Apr 30, 2026)
notes: Conceptual arc from the US District Court for the Southern District of New York (SDNY) to Culiacán, representing the April 29-30 federal indictment of Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and nine other current or former Mexican officials for Chapitos drug conspiracy and weapons charges. The first time a sitting Mexican state governor has been federally charged in US history. Co-defendants include the Mayor of Culiacán, former Security Secretary, former State Police chiefs, and a vice-fiscal — revealing a systemic state-cartel corruption network. Culmination of a sustained week of maximum US pressure (Apr 20 visa restrictions, Apr 24 OFAC sanctions, Apr 28 Los Mochis indictment preview, Apr 30 actual charges). Governor Rocha Moya denied the charges as 'a perverse strategy to violate the constitutional order.'

label: SEMAR Raids 'Mayito Flaco' Lab — Naval Base to Lab Site (May 8, 2026)
notes: Route of SEMAR (Mexican Navy) forces from the Culiacán naval base to the location of a clandestine narco-laboratory attributed to Ismael 'Mayito Flaco' Zambada Sicairos (La Mayiza emerging leader) on May 8, 2026. Lab contained centrifuges, reactors, and ~200L/20kg of synthetic drug precursors; 2,500-plant marijuana plantation incinerated. No armed confrontation. Short urban operation demonstrating SEMAR's continued intelligence-driven capability against La Mayiza infrastructure in the Culiacán battlespace. Occurred on the same day El Mayo's EDNY sentencing was postponed to July 20.

label: US Treasury OFAC — 11 Chapitos Crypto Launderers Sanctioned; 6 Ethereum Wallets Blocked (May 20, 2026)
notes: Conceptual arc from US Treasury OFAC (Washington DC) to Culiacán, representing the May 20, 2026 designation of 11 individuals and 2 entities (Gorditas Chiwas restaurant, Grupo Especial Mamba Negra security firm) tied to the Los Chapitos cash-to-crypto money laundering pipeline. Six Ethereum wallet addresses added to SDN list; pipeline converted US drug sales cash to USDT stablecoins via unlicensed OTC brokers for transfer to Mexico. Central figure: Armando de Jesus Ojeda Aviles, Los Chapitos' chief money laundering architect. Coordinated with DEA and HSI. The fourth major US financial enforcement action against the Sinaloa Cartel since April 20, 2026.

label: Mérida Sánchez Surrender Arc — Sinaloa to SDNY Manhattan (May 15, 2026)
notes: Conceptual arc from Culiacán (heart of the Chapitos bribery network Mérida Sánchez allegedly served) to the Southern District of New York courthouse in Manhattan where Gerardo Mérida Sánchez — former Sinaloa Secretary of Public Security (Sep 2023–Dec 2024) — made his initial appearance on May 15, 2026. He voluntarily surrendered in Arizona on May 11 and was transferred to Brooklyn federal detention. The first of 10 indicted Mexican officials to face US justice under the April 29, 2026 SDNY indictment package charging him with accepting $100,000/month from Los Chapitos to tip off at least 10 raids. His cooperation as a former state security chief holds significant intelligence value for future Chapitos prosecutions.

label: DOJ EDVA — Two Chinese Nationals Indicted for Sinaloa/CJNG Money Laundering (May 23, 2026)
notes: Conceptual arc from the Eastern District of Virginia (Alexandria, VA) to Culiacán, representing the May 23, 2026 unsealing of an EDVA indictment against two Chinese nationals — Ruhuan Zhen and Hongce Wu — for laundering drug proceeds for both the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG through a multi-jurisdictional network spanning November 2016 through April 2025. The network used mirror transfers, foreign bank accounts, encrypted communications, a cash serial-number verification system, and trade-based money laundering. Both defendants remain at large; maximum penalty 20 years each. Prosecuted by DOJ Criminal Division (AAG A. Tysen Duva) and DEA SAC Cindy Marx. The EDVA action is the fifth major US enforcement action against the Sinaloa Cartel's financial infrastructure in 34 days (following Apr 20 visa restrictions, Apr 24 OFAC precursor sanctions, Apr 29 SDNY indictments, May 20 OFAC crypto sanctions). Unlike the SDNY/OFAC Chapitos-focused actions, the EDVA indictment targets a Chinese-national money laundering network that simultaneously served both Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG — illustrating the broader transnational criminal ecosystem surrounding both organizations.
